Cutting losses fast isn't discipline if you're also cutting winners fast out of fear.
Most people asking for a mentor really just want someone to blame later.
A trading community can teach you patterns faster than it teaches you patience.
Backtesting proves a strategy worked. It doesn't prove you'll follow it live.
The traders who post the least about their wins are usually the ones actually winning.
Consistency gets praised more than it gets practiced.
Waiting for the perfect setup is often just fear wearing a strategy costume.
Most trading advice online is written by people selling something, not trading something.
More indicators on your chart doesn't mean more clarity. Usually it means less.
A high win rate doesn't mean a good strategy if your losers are bigger than your winners.
Trading full time isn't freedom if you're still watching every candle out of fear.
Being right about the market and making money from it are two different skills.
